chunks: Ḥammād ibn ʿUthmān narrated from Abū al-Ṣabbāḥ al-Kinānī, who said:

I said to Abū al-Ḥasan عليه السلام: “My mother gave me her share in a house as charity. So I said to her: ‘The judges do not approve this, but write it as a sale.’ She said: ‘Do from that whatever appears proper to you, and whatever you see to be permissible for you.’ So I secured it accordingly.
Then some of the heirs wanted to make me swear that I had paid this price, while I had not paid her anything. So what do you think?
He عليه السلام said: “Swear to him.”

key_terms.تَصَدَّقَتْ: she gave as charity or donation
key_terms.نَصِيبٍ: a share or portion of property
key_terms.يَسْتَحْلِفَنِي: to require me to swear an oath

ai.seo_question: What does this hadith say about swearing an oath in a property dispute involving heirs and an undocumented payment?
ai.summary: This hadith concerns a legal dispute involving a mother’s transfer of her share in a house to her son and the formal recording of that transfer as a sale. When an heir later demanded an oath regarding payment of the price, Abū al-Ḥasan عليه السلام instructed him to swear, making the report relevant to questions of property transfer, inheritance, and judicial procedure.
